title: Audio Classification — From k-NN on MFCCs to AST and BEATs

questions.question: What is the feature length returned by summarize for 13 MFCC coefficients per frame?
questions.explanation: summarize concatenates a 13-value mean with a 13-value variance vector.

questions.question: Which representation does featurize build before summarize?
options: A single raw waveform sample per class
A sequence of log-mel frames transformed into 13 DCT coefficients
A one-hot vector for the four tone labels
A complex-valued FFT with no mel filtering
questions.explanation: The pipeline is STFT magnitude, mel filterbank, log transform, then dct_ii per frame.

questions.question: How does knn select the labels that vote?
options: It samples k labels uniformly from the class dictionary
It takes the k items with the smallest raw waveform amplitude
It takes the k bank items with highest cosine similarity to q
It chooses every training item whose MFCC is exactly equal to q
questions.explanation: The indices are sorted by negative cosine and truncated to k before Counter.most_common selects a label.

questions.question: What does cosine do when an embedding has zero norm?
options: It divides by the number of MFCC frames
It returns a class label immediately
It removes the embedding from the bank
It substitutes 1e-12 for that norm to avoid division by zero
questions.explanation: Both norms use math.sqrt(...) or 1e-12, keeping the score calculation finite.

questions.question: Why does the synthetic classifier use tones at 200, 400, 800, and 1600 Hz?
options: They create four labeled frequency classes that the MFCC features can separate
They are four speech languages with identical spectra
They ensure every class has the same text transcript
They make the waveform contain no periodic structure
questions.explanation: The frequencies define the four class labels; noise adds variation while preserving the class-defining tone.

questions.question: Why would accuracy alone be insufficient for an imbalanced audio dataset?
options: Accuracy automatically reports latency and memory for every class
A majority-class predictor can look strong while missing minority events, so per-class or macro metrics are needed
Accuracy is undefined whenever labels are strings
An imbalanced dataset makes cosine similarity impossible
questions.explanation: The lesson highlights class imbalance: aggregate accuracy can hide poor recall on rare sounds.
